jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Case Closed
jokes.joke: I’d be the worst detective. I’m so lazy I’d show up to a crime scene, see the chalk outline, and go, “Great, somebody already traced him.” Then I’d arrest the victim for being the only guy who couldn’t explain where he was.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Case Closed
jokes.joke: I tried being a detective for a week. Day one, I found a crucial lead. Day two, I lost it. Day three, I found it again in my jacket. Day four, I decided the jacket was a suspect. By Friday I'd arrested my own coat, written up a full report, and closed the case. The coat got six months. I got a commendation. Justice, apparently, is just paperwork with confidence.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Superhuman Strength
seedTermsUsed: A loved one being put in harm's way
jokes.joke: They say in an emergency, adrenaline takes over and you can lift a car off your spouse. But I know myself, and I am deeply, profoundly lazy. If my wife gets pinned under a sedan, my first instinct isn't superhuman strength. It's sliding a throw pillow under her head and whispering, 'Let's just see where we're at in the morning.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Couch Detective
jokes.joke: You know, I tried being a detective, but I'm way too lazy for the job. Last week my neighbor hired me to find his stolen bike. I 'investigated' from my recliner for three hours, then told him it was probably gone forever. Turns out I was using it as a footrest the whole time. He fired me on the spot. Best case I ever closed without getting up.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Detective Instincts
jokes.joke: I realized I’m basically a bumbling detective the other day. I tried to find my missing keys, spent ten minutes interrogating the dog, then discovered them in my own pocket. And instead of feeling relieved, I just thought, “Great… even my crimes are lazy.”

scores.comment: Amusing coat escalation and a solid closing idea, but the lazy seed is not clearly used as a concept.
Strong concrete emergency premise, clean lazy reversal, and the final line lands with real stage rhythm.
Clear and readable with a decent footrest reveal, though the detective-lazy pairing feels familiar.
Clean first-person form and fits the seeds, but the missing-keys setup is familiar and the punchline is mild.
Clean escalation, the second sentence lands hard. Arresting the victim for having no alibi is a sharp, non-obvious turn that earns the laugh without telegraphing it. Tight and stageworthy.

Best in batch. The 'throw pillow' image is specific and perfectly lazy, and 'let's just see where we're at in the morning' is a genuinely funny final line that a human would repeat. Surprising angle, clean build, no wasted words.

Competent and the footrest reveal is a solid enough turn, but the setup is long and the 'best case I ever closed without getting up' ending tries to do too much at once. Readable filler; not memorable.
The key-in-pocket setup is extremely familiar, and 'even my crimes are lazy' is more of a summary than a punchline. The joke does not land beyond a mild nod of recognition.
The chalk outline setup is a bit cartoonish, but the second punchline arresting the victim is an excellent, unexpected turn that lands well.
Reads more like a whimsical story than stand-up. The premise escalates into absurdity, and the final line feels like a generic essay takeaway rather than a punchline.
The physical logic of using a neighbor's stolen bike as a recliner footrest without noticing completely breaks the necessary suspension of disbelief.
Relies on tired tropes of lost keys and interrogating pets, recites the seed term literally, and the final punchline makes no sense as losing keys is not a crime.
Solid pun setup with a dark twist, but relies on familiar tropes.
Meandering bit that builds to a mild, generic closer.
Strong premise, vivid lazy subversion of hero trope, lands cleanly.
Compact self-own with a decent tag, but predictable.
Solid premise with a clear turn, but the punchline is mild and a bit expected.
Fun escalation and clean storytelling, but the final turn lands more as whimsy than a sharp laugh.
Clear premise, relatable angle, and a good final image; lands a real laugh though not quite standout.
Competent and coherent with a tidy turn, but the humor is predictable and the ending is gentle rather than punchy.
